hits.73: Where upstream inflow drives a substantial part of the inundation we inject daily GloFAS-v4 reanalysis discharge (Harrigan et al. 2020) at named point sources, interpolated to the model clock: enabled for Pineios (four inflow points) and Strymonas (two, at the Kerkini outlet and Angitis), disabled for Mandra, whose ~10 km² sub-catchments fall below the GloFAS grid. Each run uses an antecedent spin-up — 1 d for the single-burst Mandra event, 7 d for Pineios and Strymonas — the longer window wetting the unsaturated zone so the curve-number response reflects catchment wetness at onset, essential for Storm Daniel's high antecedent runoff coefficients Dimitriou et al. 2024.
hits.92: EMS validation uses the wide-Thessaly configuration (the event is in Section 2.3): a 98 × 80 km domain at 150-m base grid with 4× sub-grid (37.5 m effective), 262,465 active cells to zmax = 400 m, with water-level boundary cells at the Thermaikos outlet (inverse-barometer ~25 cm). The run uses all five upgrades: gauge-bias-corrected IMERG (resolving the embedded Pelion convection ERA5 smooths); ERA5 wind and pressure; SCS-CN with AMC-II→III scaling for the saturated post-August soil; and GloFAS-v4 discharge at four reach points. The GloFAS-v4 reanalysis at these reaches peaks ~3580 m³ s⁻¹, ~50–80% above the ~1900–2300 m³ s⁻¹ observed at Larissa (Dimitriou et al. 2024) (a documented medicane over-prediction); the canonical run, however, injected a near-constant placeholder series at these points, and an audit re-run with the full time-varying GloFAS series (peak 118 m³ s⁻¹ at the lowest-zb channel cell; Appendix B) returned identical headline metrics — confirming the Pineios flood is rainfall-dominated and the edge-cell inflows are negligible against the in-domain runoff. A 7-day spin-up wets the basin to the high antecedent runoff coefficients of Dimitriou et al. 2024 (simulation 03–11 September).
hits.125: The domain spans ~26 × 28 km on a 569 × 542 grid at 50 m (162,335 active cells), with 4 × 4 sub-grid sampling giving 12.5 m effective resolution — enough to capture the central Mandra street geometry to first order without a dual-drainage solver. Three upgrades are applied over the baseline rain-on-grid run: gauge-bias-corrected IMERG Final V07 precipitation; ERA5 wind and pressure (a ~5 cm inverse-barometer term at the Saronic boundary, kept for protocol consistency); and SCS-CN disabled. The bias correction is essential — over the 14–15 November window the raw IMERG watershed-mean total is only ~23 mm against the gauge-based 158–300 mm, the convective core being sub-grid at the 0.1° (~11 km) IMERG resolution; a ×8.55 factor over that window scales it to 200 mm, after which the peak intensity (~44 mm h⁻¹, maximum-cell ~109 mm h⁻¹) agrees with radar (Lagouvardos et al. 2017). Infiltration is disabled per the Appendix A sweep — any non-zero CN absorbs the rainfall and suppresses the flood, while the post-fire catchment is near-impervious. GloFAS is not injected; the simulation covers 13–18 November after a 1-day spin-up.
hits.154: The domain spans ~100 × 90 km on a 611 × 690 grid at 150 m (Table 2), with a ~4666 km² active mask from below Kerkini to the gulf and along the Angitis. Enhanced forcing combines all five upgrades: IMERG precipitation; ERA5 wind and pressure with the inverse-barometer term at the gulf boundary; SCS-CN infiltration (HSG-B, AMC-II) with a 7-day spin-up; and GloFAS-v4 discharge at two inflow points — the Kerkini outlet capturing the spillway release and the Angitis confluence.

time_management.text: The required model runtime can be specified by setting a reference date (tref), start date (tstart) and stop date (tstop).

tspinup.text: Duration of spinup period after tstart, where the water level variation at the boundary is dampened, between values in the `bzsfile' input and the value of `zsini' (even if using rstfile as initial condition)

spinup_meteo.text: Option to also apply spinup to the meteo forcing, default is off (0)

zsini.text: Initial water level in entire domain - where above bed level.

dis_time_ref.text: Then in the file `sfincs.dis' the discharge time-series are specified per input location. Times are specified in seconds with respect to SFINCS' internal reference time `tref', as specified in sfincs.inp.

rain_time_ref.text: Rain input in mm/hr, times are specified in seconds with respect to SFINCS' internal reference time `tref', as specified in sfincs.inp.

restart_spinup.text: In order to run SFINCS without spinup of water levels in a subsequent simulation, the waterlevels at the final time step of the former can be saved as binary-file using either the specification of a specific time you want to have the restartfile
